name: Pyramids of Giza
label: GIZA PYRAMIDS
description: Three immense stone pyramids rise from the desert west of the Nile. Our pilot points out the broken casing high on their slopes.
clue: From Alexandria, follow the coast east to the Rosetta mouth of the Nile, then sail upriver. The pyramids stand on the western bank near Cairo.
history: Old Kingdom monuments, third millennium BCE.

name: Citadel of Qaitbay
label: QAITBAY CITADEL
description: A pale stone fortress guards Alexandria's harbor, built on the site of the ancient lighthouse.
clue: At Alexandria, look for the fortress guarding the western harbor. Sail close to the old Pharos shore.
history: Built 1477–1479; the ancient lighthouse no longer stands in 1522.

name: Leptis Magna
label: LEPTIS MAGNA
description: Weathered arches and columns stand among the sands beside an ancient harbor. This was once a great Roman city.
clue: Sail east along the Libyan coast from Tripoli. Beyond the next headland, Roman columns stand near the sea.
history: Ancient city with major Roman monuments; largely abandoned by the medieval period.

name: The Colosseum
label: COLOSSEUM
description: Our shore party sketches Rome's great oval amphitheater. Rows of arches survive above the fallen stones of its southern wall.
clue: Between Pisa and Naples, follow the coast to the mouth of the Tiber. A shore party can seek Rome's ancient amphitheater inland.
history: Roman amphitheater inaugurated in 80 CE; represented as a ruin rather than its intact ancient form.

name: Rock of Gibraltar
label: GIBRALTAR
description: A steep limestone ridge towers above the northern side of the strait. The Atlantic winds meet the Mediterranean here.
clue: East of Seville, pass through the narrow entrance to the Mediterranean. A great pale rock rises on the northern shore opposite Ceuta.

name: Mount Vesuvius
label: VESUVIUS
description: A dark volcanic cone rises above the Bay of Naples. The slopes are quiet today, but the local pilots tell grim stories of the mountain.
clue: Sail into the Bay of Naples. The volcanic mountain rises inland to the east of the harbor.
history: Natural volcano, drawn without an invented continuous eruption.

name: Kilwa Kisiwani
label: KILWA KISIWANI
description: Coral-stone walls and a domed mosque overlook an island harbor. Local sailors speak of Kilwa's long trade in gold across the Indian Ocean.
clue: On the East African coast between Mozambique and Mombasa, search the islands for Kilwa's coral-stone buildings.
history: Medieval Swahili trading city; its great mosque and palace predate 1522. It is portrayed as a settlement, not solely modern ruins.

name: Borobudur
label: BOROBUDUR
description: A shore expedition returns from central Java with drawings of a stepped stone sanctuary. Small bell-shaped stupas rise through the vegetation.
clue: Follow Java's coast east from Sunda. Inland in central Java, guides tell of a great stepped sanctuary among the hills.
history: Eighth–ninth century sanctuary, partly covered by vegetation before its nineteenth-century clearance. Inland visits are an exploration abstraction.

name: Great Buddha of Kamakura
label: GREAT BUDDHA
description: A great bronze Buddha sits beneath the open sky near Kamakura. The hall that once sheltered it has been lost.
clue: Follow Japan's southern coast east from Sakai. Near Kamakura, a great bronze Buddha sits close to the shore.
history: Construction began in 1252; the hall was lost by 1498, so the statue stands outdoors in 1522.

name: Moai of Rapa Nui
label: RAPA NUI MOAI
description: Tall stone figures look inland from the coast of a lonely Pacific island. Our sailors sketch their long faces and heavy brows.
clue: Far west of the Chilean coast lies a small, isolated island. Look for stone figures along its eastern shore.
history: Moai carving and ahu construction predate 1522. The stylized group does not reproduce the modern restored arrangement at Ahu Tongariki.
